TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng.
President DATE: March 20, 2024 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of a real estate transaction with the East Farm Commercial Fisheries Center and the Commercial Fisheries Research Foundatio n, and the negotiation and execution of all documents relating to such transaction Purpose of Submittal: The University is seeking approval from the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees for a real estate transaction on substantially the terms set forth in the enclosed Term Sheet, by which URI would license a portion of land located at 61 C East Farm Road in Kingston to the East Farm Com mercial Fisheries Center and the Commercial Fisheries Research Foundation (jointly and severally, “Commercial Fisheries”) , for purposes of allowing the Commercial Fisheries to construct, own, maintain, and operate a building on the site.
Points to Consider: This transaction serves to continue a relationship with the Commercial Fisheries that first began in 2003 .

The Commercial Fisheries currently occupy and maintain the building at 61 B East Farm Road in Kingston for office and conference room space, and this transaction would allow them to expand by constructing a new 50ft x 30ft building for additional office and storage space on the adjacent 61 C East Farm Road site.
There is an existing building (the Quonset Hut) located at 61 C East Farm Road, which the Commercial Fisheries would be responsible for demolishing prior to commencing construction.
Demolition, construction, maintenance, and operations will be paid for by the Commercial Fisheries.
Recommendation: I recommend that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve a real estate transaction with the East Farm Commercial Fisheries Center and the Commercial Fisheries Research Foundation, jointly and severally, on substantially the terms outlined in the enclosed Term Sheet.
This recommendation is based on a thorough review by and with the appropriate stakeholders.
Supporting Information: Please see enclosed Term Sheet.

Proposed Motion of the Board: THAT, the Board of Trustees hereby approves licensing real estate at 61 C East Farm Road to the East Farm Commercial Fisheries Center and Commercial Fisheries Research Foundation , jointly and severally, on substantially the terms outlined in the enclosed T erm Sheet, and that the Board Chair, President, and Vice President of Administration and Finance are each individually authorized , for and on behalf of the University and the Board of Trustees, to negotiate and execute a Real Estate License Agreement and a ny other documents relating to such transaction on substantially the terms outlined in the enclosed Term Sheet, with any such changes and additional terms as are deemed necessary by the person executing the same.

East Farm Commercial Fisheries Center and The Commercial Fisheries Research Foundation Real Estate License Agreement Term Sheet Date: March 12, 2024 Real Estate Matter: Real Estate License Agreement Lessee/Licensee/Tenant: East Farm Commercial Fisheries Center Frederick Mattera, Executive Director Address: PO Box 5191 Wakefield, RI 02880 and Lessee/Licensee/Tenant: The Commercial Fisheries Research Foundation N.

David Bethoney, Executive Director Address: PO Box 278 Saunderstown, RI 02874 Lessor/Licensor/Landlord: University of Rhode Island for itself and on behalf of its Board of Trustees Address: 73 Upper College Road Kingston, RI 02881 Location/Building: Building 61 B, East Farm Road, Kingston RI and a portion of land at East Farm Road, where building 61 C East Farm Road, Kingston, RI is currently located Room/Lot: The entirety of the building located 61 B, East Farm Road, Kingston, RI identified as building 9, Plat 32-1 Lot 12, in the town of South Kingstown and a portion of the land located at East Farm Road, identified as building 10, Plat 32-1 Lot 12, in the town of South Kingstown (Exhibit A) the “Licensed Premises” Square Footage/Acreage: 2,392 sq. ft. building 61 B, East Farm Road and approximately 1500 sq. ft. of land near the footprint of the Quonset Hut at 61 C East Farm Road Description of Use: In order to support the URI-Licensee Collaborative Relationship relative to projects and initiatives that mutually benefit research and education in areas such as marine ecology, fisheries, commercial fishing, and offshore wind projects, the licensee will have (i) continued use of building 61 B, East Farm Road by the Licensee for offices and conferencing; (ii) rights to demolish the Quonset Hut located at 61 C East Farm Road;

(iii) and authorization to construct, own, maintain, and operate a new building (“Building”) for storage and additional office space.
Term: 10-year term, commencing on final approval by the Rhode Island State Properties Committee Renewal Option(s): Up to an additional 10 years.
Such renewal will need to be negotiated prior to the expiration of the original term.
Commencement Date: Upon final approval by the Rhode Island State Properties Committee Expiration Date: 10 years from commencement date (2034) Occupancy Date: Ongoing occupying of 61 B East Farm Road under the current Lease Agreement that expires on December 31, 2025.
Occupancy of Building at 61 C East Farm Road will be upon obtaining a certificate of occupancy Base Rent: Base rent is waived as the Licensee will construct the Building, which will revert to the Licensor at the end of the term, and the Licensee will continue to maintain the premises located at 61 B East Farm Road Additional Rent: None Security Deposit: None Sublease: Not allowed without seeking an amendment and approval from the Licensor.

Assignment: Upon consent by the Licensor and approval by the Rhode Island State Properties Committee if required Access: Licensee will have access to the Licensed Premises at all times Utilities: Licensee is responsible for connection to sewer and water of the Building and for the cost of utilities at that Building by submetering.
Licensee will pay for utilities at 61 B East Farm based on the overall campus average calculated using the average of the previous three fiscal years divided by total campus building square footage.
Licensee has the option of submetering at 61 B East Farm at their expense.
Maintenance/Repairs: Licensee is responsible for all maintenance & repairs to Licensed Premises, including, but not limited to exterior snow removal and treatment of entranceways and sidewalks, minor landscaping and interior custodial/housekeeping.
Licensor is responsible for snow plowing and treatment of parking lots, grass cutting, exterior trash receptables.

Alterations/Construction: Licensee is permitted to demolish and construct a Building located at 61 C East Farm Road, per plans consistent with the standard Licensor University’s requirements and schedule submitted and approved by the Licensor’s Vice President for Administration and Finance or their designee.
Licensee shall submit any changes to design, construction, or schedule for review and approval by the Vice President for Administration and Finance or their designee, approval of which will not be unreasonably withheld.
Upon completion of construction, the Licensee will provide to the Licensor’s Vice President for Administration and Finance or their designee as built drawings and a copy of the certificate of occupancy.

Financing Requirements: Agreement allows Licensee to finance the demolition of the existing building and construction of the Building.
Licensee is not permitted to commence work on the Licensed Premises until documentation has been provided to the Licensor’s Vice President of Administration and Finance or their designee to show that the work is fully funded or financed and will be completed per the schedule provided.
Insurance Requirements: As stipulated and approved by the Licensor University’s Risk Management Office Hazardous Materials: Any introduction of hazardous materials to the Licensed Premises requires prior written approval from the Licensor University’s Environmental Health and Safety Office and will be subject to Licensor’s requirements based on the hazardous materials proposed at the time.
Termination Clause: Right to Acquire Title: Licensor has the right to acquire title and full ownership of the Building and other fixtures and improvements at any time prior to Expiration Date, with one hundred and eighty days prior written notice, and by paying the fair market value of the Building.

For Cause: Licensor may terminate if Licensee fails to pay taxes and assessments, loans or financial obligations, any reimbursements due to the Licensor University pursuant to this agreement, correct deficiencies to the building, commence or complete construction in accordance with this agreement, or fail to correct or cure any material breach of terms and conditions of this agreement within 30 days.
Licensee may terminate prior to the commencement of any construction on the Building.
Additional Considerations: This agreement replaces and supersedes a prior Lease Agreement for the facilities at 61 B East Farm Road, dated December 2, 2003 and extended through two Amendments; Amendment One, dated November 10, 2009 extending the term to December 31, 2013 and Amendment Two, dated December 21, 2010 extending the term to December 31, 2020 with the option to extend an additional five years, which was exercised concluding with a final termination date of December 31, 2025. 61 C East Farm Road, Kingston is a university-owned Quonset Hut placed on East Farm around 1930.
This building has deteriorated to the point of being unusable by the University.

On February 22, 2024 the University received approval from the State of Rhode Island Historical Preservation & Heritage Commission (RIHPHC), after review for historical value, to demolish this existing structure.
Licensee is responsible for own due diligence in the demolition of the existing building and construction of the Building including connections to utilities.

Points to Consider: The Financial Strategy and Planning team has conducted an analysis of our projected FY24 performance versus budget and presented in the enclosure is a range of outcomes, from least likely to most likely. We cannot assume that one -time inflows/expense reductions will continue to offset permanent expenses. The enclosure also gives a brief update on the IBB implementation, highlighting that we are currently in the process of building the model and engaging in extensive stakeholder engagement throughout the university. TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng.
President DATE: March 20, 2024 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of a real estate transaction with the Tomaquag Indian Memorial Museum, and the negotiation and execution of all documents relating to such transaction Purpose of Submittal: The University is seeking approval from the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees for a real estate transaction on substantially the terms set forth in the enclosed Term Sheet, by which URI would license 3.10 acres of the parcel of land at 3045 Kingstown Road, identified as AP 23-1, Lot 1 in the Town of South Kingstown, to the Tomaquag Indian Memorial Museum for purposes of allowing the Museum to construct, own, maintain, and operate a commercial museum building on the site.
Points to Consider: URI and the Museum are currently parties to a Real Estate License Agreement for a site on Ministerial Road.

As part of this transaction, the Museum would move to the site at 3045 Kingstown Road and the license for Ministerial Road would terminate .
There is an existing building at 3045 Kingstown Road (formerly known as the International Scholar-Athlete Hall of Fame), which is unoccupiable due to the deteriorated condition.
Allowing the Museum to construct, own, maintain, and operate a commercial museum at 3045 Kingstown Road will improve the condition of the licensed property and will be nefit the University and the surrounding community.
Recommendation: I recommend that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve a real estate transaction with the Tomaquag Indian Memorial Museum on substantially the terms outlined in the enclosed Term Sheet .
This recommendation is based on a thorough review by and with the appropriate stakeholders.
Supporting Information: Please see enclosed Term Sheet.

Proposed Motion of the Board: THAT, the Board of Trustees hereby approves licensing real estate at 30 45 Kingstown Road to the Tomaquag Indian Museum on substantially the terms outlined in the enclosed Term Sheet , and that the Board Chair, President, and Vice President of Administration and Finance are each individually authorized, for and on behalf of the University and the Board of Trustees, to negotiate and execute a Real Estate License Agreement and any other documents relating to such transaction on substantially the terms outlined in the enclosed Term Sheet, with any such changes and additional terms as are deemed necessary and appropriate by the person executing the same.

Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: April 4, 2024 SUBJECT: Discussion Item: Classification and Compensation Study Purpose of Submittal: Update the Committee on a recently launched classification and compensation study for URI’s non-classified staff.
Classified civil service positions, faculty, and graduate assistant positions will not be included as part of this review.
Points to Consider: URI is committed to fostering an inclusive, people -centered culture and continuing our efforts to attract, recognize, and retain outstanding staff and faculty.
In support of this strategic priority, we have recently launched a comprehensive review and revision of our classification and compensation structure for non- classified staff.
Huron Consulting Group was secured to support this study through a competitive Request for Proposal process.

Our goal is to develop a well -structured, transparent, and equitable compensation platform that provides clear pathways for advancement, rewards outstanding performance, and supports competitive compensation.
This modernization of our classification and compensation structure will result in a cohesive compensation philosophy, formal job architecture and career pathing, new job profiles more clearly connected to the competitive market, and policies and processes to sustain improvement.
The study is expected to take up to one year to complete.
Review and implementation of the study will be a multi- year effort, and we will work closely with the relevant staff and unions throughout the process.
Supporting Information: See enclosure.
